JUDGMENT
The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- for the death of Sri.Manjegowda in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioners' case are as under:
2.

That, on 25.11.2024 at about 9.00 p.m., the deceased Sri.Manjegowda was proceeding as a pedestrian on Sumanahalli ring road, Bangalore city, when he reached opposite to Indian Oil Petrol pump and Green residence, at that time, driver of Heavy Goods Carrier Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-05/AH-0098 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, came at high speed and dashed against the deceased.
Due to which, Manjegowda sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately he was shifted to Kenganar Hospital, Kachohalli Cross, Magadi, after first aid, he was shifted to Victoria hospital, Bengalore, wherein he died during the course of treatment.

Thereafter,
post mortem was conducted and dead body was handed over to the petitioners.

Subsequently, the petitioners have spent Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical expenses, transportation of dead body,
funeral and obsequies ceremonies of the deceased and other incidental expenses.
3. It is further stated in the petition that, prior to the accident, the deceased was working as Security and earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
Due to the untimely death of the deceased, life of the petitioners are put to lot of mental agony and untold misery.
4. It is stated that, the accident was occurred due to the negligent act of the driver of the Heavy Goods Carrier Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-05/AH-0098.
Hence, Kamakshipalya Police have registered a criminal case against driver of said offending vehicle in Cr.No.172/2024.
As such, the respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

Hence,
this petition.
5. In response to the notice, respondent No.1 & 2 have appeared through their respective counsel and filed their written statements.

sentences.text: In the written statement, the respondent No.1 has contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.

Further, this respondent is the owner of the Heavy Goods Carrier Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-05/AH-0098 and he got insured said vehicle with respondent No.2 and the policy was valid as on the date of accident.
The driver had valid D.L. as on the date of accident.
Hence, respondent No.2 has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
There is no fault the part of the driver of offending vehicle.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and relationship between deceased with the petitioners.
Ultimately contended that the claim of the petitioners is highly excessive, exorbitant and arbitrary.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition against this respondent.
7. In the written statement, the respondent No.2 has contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.

Further, this respondent has admitted about issuance of insurance policy in respect of Heavy Goods Carrier Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-05/AH-0098 and the liability of this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.

It is also contention of the respondent No.2 that, the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective D.L. as on the date of the accident, hence there is a violation of terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
It is the defence of the respondent No.2 that, the accident was occurred due to negligence on the part of the deceased himself.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and relationship between deceased with the petitioners.
Ultimately contended that the claim of the petitioners is highly excessive, exorbitant and arbitrary.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition against this respondent.

8. On the basis of the rival pleadings of both the parties, this court had framed the following issues:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that Sro.Manjegowda died due to the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident which took place on 25.11.2024 at about 09.00 p.m opposite Indian oil petrol pump and green residence, Sumanahalli out ring road,
Benglauru, due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Heavy Goods Carrier Lorry bearing registration No.KA-05-AH-0098 in an actionable negligence?
2) Whether the petitioners prove that, they are legal heirs and were depending upon the income of the deceased?
3) Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?

If so, at what rate and from whom?
 4) What order or award?

9. In order to substantiate their case, the petitioner No.1 got examined herself as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P16.
10.
On the other hand, the respondents have not led any rebuttal evidence in order to disprove the case of the petitioners.

sentences.text: Heard the arguments of both the counsel.
Perused the materials available on record.

12. My findings to the above issues as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: In the Affirmative Issue No.3: Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.4: As per final order, for the following:
R E A S O N S ISSUE No.1:-
13.

It is the specific case of the petitioners that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the Heavy Goods Carrier Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-05/AH-0098, the alleged accident had taken place.
Consequently, Manjegowda died in the said accident.
As such, the petitioners have filed this claim petition against the respondents.
14. On the contrary, the respondents though not disputed the accident and the death of Manjegowda, but strongly disputed the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
15. In such a situation, it is necessary to go through the evidence available on record, in order to come to the proper conclusion with respect to the above point in issue.
On going through the above issue, burden is on the petitioners to prove the same on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities.
16. The petitioners in order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 has examined as PW1.
In her examination-in-chief by way of affidavit has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
PW1 in support of her oral evidence has relied upon the police documents at Ex.
P1 to Ex

Ex. P1-true copy of the F.I.R, Ex.P2- true copy of first information statement given by Abhishek M., Ex.P3-true copy of Spot mahazar, Ex.P4-true copy of spot sketch, Ex.P5- true copy of inquest report, Ex.P6-true copy of PM report, Ex.P7-notice u/s 133 of MV Act,

Ex.P8-reply to notice u/s 133 of MV Act,
Ex.P9-true copy of IMV report and Ex.P10-true copy of charge sheet 17.

On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by Abhishek M., the S.H.O. of Kamakshipalya police have registered the case against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Section 281, 125(b) of BNS Act.

Upon investigation, the I.O. has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section and 281, 106(1) of BNS Act.
18.

Though, the respondents have disputed the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, but not examined either the driver of the offending vehicle or any of the independent eye witness to prove its contention.

sentences.text: Apart from this, at the time of cross- examination of PW1, no material answers culled out to believe the defenses of the respondent No.2 about the denial of allegation made against the driver of the offending vehicle.
20. In the light of the evidence placed by petitioners, I am of the view that, the petitioners have placed satisfactory and acceptable evidence to prove the above issue.

Hence, I hold that, the accident was occurred purely on the part of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Heave Goods Carrier Lorry bearing No.KA-05-AH-0098 and in the said accident, Manjegowda succumbed to the injuries.
Accordingly, I am answering the Issue No.1 is in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.2 & 3;
21.

Now coming to the point of quantum of compensation for which, the petitioners are entitled is concerned, every legal representative who suffers on account of the death of a person, due to a motor vehicle accident, should have remedy for realization of compensation.

Since in the death case,
the legal heirs are the claimants.
In the case on hand, the relationship of deceased with the petitioners is not in dispute.

At the same time, the documents produced by the petitioners, to prove their relationship with the deceased marked at Ex.P13 to Ex.P16 Aadhar cards of the petitioners and the deceased, have not been disputed by the other side.
The recitals of the above documents clearly speak about the relationship between the petitioners and the deceased.

22. Another aspect to be considered herein that, on going through the particulars of the petitioners mentioned in the cause title of the petition reflected that, the petitioner No.1 being the wife has lost her husband and the petitioner No.2 to 4 are the children of the deceased have lost their love and affection of their father, who was the backbone of the family.
Hence, it is crystal clear that, the petitioners were dependents on the deceased during his lifetime.
23. In the case on hand, no doubt the petitioner No.2 & 3 are children of the deceased Manjegowda.
According to them, they were dependents to the deceased petitioner during his lifetime.
No contra materials are available on record to show that, they were not dependents to their father during his lifetime.
Here, it is necessary to discuss the point that, father place an important role in the family.
All the children, one or the other way defendants to their parents whether they are minors or majors, married or unmarried.
But the percentage of disability may be varied from one person to another person.
During the minority of the child, dependency is more on the parents.
After the marriage of the children, the percentage of disability is less on the parents, if compare with the minor children.

24. In the case on hand, by looking to the age criteria though they are major sons, they could have dependents to their parents not only economically, but, in connection with love and affection during his lifetime.
Hence, the petitioners can be presumed as dependents to their father during his lifetime in the absence of contra materials from the other side.

25. The Division Bench of Supreme Court, in National Insurance Company Limited V/S Birender and Others stated that, a major and earning son has a right to claim compensation under Motor Savitha vs S K Aagro Techh on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175024579/
5 Vehicle Act.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Motor Savitha vs S K Aagro Techh on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this case, by referring the case of Manjuri Bera, stated that, even if there is no loss of dependency, the claimant if he was a legal representative will be entitled to compensation.

Even the major married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation, and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application,
irrespective of the fact, whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only."
26. The petitioners herein, have placed Aadhar card marked at Ex.P14 to prove the actual age of the deceased as on the date of the accident.
On going through the said document, the year of birth of the deceased has been mentioned as 1970.
The accident occurred on 25.11.2024.
Therefore, as on the date of accident, the deceased was aged about 53 years.
For his age, multiplier '11' is applicable as per the ratio in "Sarala Verma" Case.
27. In connection with the work of the deceased, in the main petition and also in the evidence of PW1 stated that, deceased was working as a security and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
But in support of definite income of the deceased, there is no iota of documents to show that he was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
In such a situation, as per law notional income has to be taken into consideration.
Hence, the income of the deceased is apt to be taken as Rs.16,500/- p.m., which will meet the ends of justice.

28. Apart from this, it is also relevant to discuss, that the Honourable Supreme Court in the decision reported in, 2018 SAR (Civil) 81. National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others,
"

entities.text: 2018 SAR (Civil) 81. National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was observed that, "While determining the income, an addition of 50 per cent of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The addition should be 30 per cent, if the age of the deceased was between 40 and 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 and 60 years, the addition should be 15 per cent.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.
In case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40 per cent of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 year.
An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years.

An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 and 50 years and 10 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 50-60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.

The established income means the income minus the tax component. "
29.

Having considered the above, as per law laid down in the above case, in connection with the deduction of personal and living expenses is concerned, it is settled that, "where the deceased was married, the deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased should be one third (1/3 rd) where the number of dependent family members is 2 to 3, 1/4th where the number of dependent family member is 4 to 6 and one fifth (1/5 th ) where the number of the dependent family members exceeds six."
30. In the light of the above proposition, in the case on hand, there are three persons were depending upon the income of the deceased.

Hence, as per the principle laid down by the Savitha vs S K Aagro Techh on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175024579/
6

sentences.text: Honourable Supreme Court in Sarala Verma Case at para No.14, 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses out of the total compensation.
31. In the present case, deceased was aged about 53 years as on the date of the accident.
For this age multiplier "11" is applicable.

And by relying on the aforesaid principle laid down in the Pranay Sethi's case with respect to the age of the deceased and also on going through the nature of the occupation forthcoming in the petition averments, it is evident that, the deceased herein is not having permanent job and accurate income for consideration.
As such, deceased was comes under the between age of 50 to 60 years, 10% income of the deceased has to be taken into account towards future prospects.
Therefore, by considering the earning of the deceased as Rs.16,500/- per month.
Annual income of the deceased was Rs.1,98,000/- per year.
Along with this, the future prospects of 10% is to be taken in to consideration, then the annual income of the deceased comes to (Rs.1,98,000+19,800) = Rs.2,17,800/-.
And 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses in the income of the deceased.

Thus, net loss of income comes to Rs.1,45,200/-
(Rs.2,17,800-Rs.72,600).

This income has to be multiplied by multiplier "11" which comes to Rs.15,97,200/-.
32.

Apart from this aspect, in connection with the loss of estate, consortium and with respect to the funeral expenses to calculate the quantum of the compensation under the aforesaid heads, it is relevant to note herein the following authority;
2018 SAR (Civil) 81. National Insurance Company Limited.
V/ s Pranay Sethi and others
, The Hon'ble Apex Court discussed various aspects in connection with the claim petition filed by the claimants for compensation.

And also observed that while determining the claim petition, the reasonable figures on conventional heads, viz., loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/-, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
The aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.

33. By relying upon the above said decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, the amount of Rs.18,150/- is awarded under the head loss of estate and Rs.18,150/- is awarded towards funeral expenses and also by placing reliance upon the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Company Limited v/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram & Others, the amount of Rs.48,400/- each is awarded to the petitioner No.1 to 3 under the head loss of consortium.

Medical expenses;
34.
After the accident deceased was shifted to Kanganar Hospital, Bengaluru, for which the petitioners have spent Rs.1,15,286/-, the said bills marked at Ex.P12 along with prescriptions at Ex.P11.
There are no contra materials available on record to disprove the medical bills.
Hence, it is just and proper to award Rs.1,15,286/- towards medical expenses.
35. Considering the above facts and circumstances of the case and for the above reason, I am of the opinion that, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation under the following heads.

(Rupees eighteen lakhs ninety three thousand nine hundred and eighty six only), along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Hon'ble High court of Karnataka in MFA No. 103557/2016, Between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S.

LIABILITY:
37.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioners that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Heavy Goods Carrier Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-05/AH-0098, alleged accident had taken place.
The evidence given by the petitioners in connection with the issue No.1, remained unshaken.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the R.C.
owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
38. As per records insurance policy was valid from 3.11.2024 to 2.11.2025.
The alleged accident had taken place on 25.11.2024.
Therefore, the respondent No.2 being the insurance company is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Hence, respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition, till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 answered in the Affirmative and the issue No.3 is answered partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.4:
39.

In view of my due discussions on Issue Nos.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following;
 O R D E R

The claim petition filed by the Savitha vs S K Aagro Techh on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175024579/
8 petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

sentences.text: The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.18,93,986/- (Rupees eighteen lakhs ninety three thousand nine hundred and eighty six only), along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the petitioner No.1 is entitled the share of 80%, the petitioner No.2 & 3 are entitled the share of 10% each.

After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest of petitioner No.1, shall deposit 40% of her share in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank of her choice for a period of 3 years and remaining 60% shall be released to her through due process of law.
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest of petitioner No.2 & 3, since the amount is very meagre, entire amount shall be released to the petitioner through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

In such a situation, as per law notional income has to be taken into consideration.
Hence, the income of the deceased is apt to be taken as Rs.16,500/- p.m., which will meet the ends of justice.
And by relying on the aforesaid principle laid down in the Pranay Sethi's case with respect to the age of the deceased and also on going through the nature of the occupation forthcoming in the petition averments, it is evident that, the deceased herein is not having permanent job and accurate income for consideration.
As such, deceased was comes under the between age of 50 to 60 years, 10% income of the deceased has to be taken into account towards future prospects.
